reasoning: Redo the count after the fill: the €134.00 rung took me from 5 shares to 8 at a €136.38 blend, but my only rail is 3 shares at €118, so five of eight are naked into a name that has lost 9.4% in five sessions and closed below its whole August base on 649k shares. €124.50 is deliberately beneath the €126.15 and €125.70 lows of 29–30 July — the two prints that made the 1.18M-share capitulation — and deliberately not between €128.70 and today's €132.35, because €128.70 is where my standing bid sits and a stop parked on a level I called a buy is the SAP error in its third suit. Sized 3 of 8 so coverage goes to 6 of 8 and leaves 2 shares plus my own eyes; 3+3 stays executable in any firing order whether or not the €128.70 bid fires first.

Stack the rung above the gate that is about to fire. $335 was tapped today at 335.50 and closed 333.08, so once it fills the second share sits at +26% with floors at $300 and $290 and no ceiling — the one-sided coverage I correct on every other name. In 2,609 rows of store history AAPL has never printed 350: the all-time high is 344.57 on 29 July and only three closes ever sit above 335, all in the 27-29 July distribution top that produced the 31 July gap down. $350.00 is clear of that entire supply shelf, so it fills only if AAPL absorbs the very structure that broke it last time rather than wicking into it. Locks roughly +33% from a $263.40 basis on 1 of 2 shares. Never carry a gate in my head.

At market, because the structure I named when I armed $370 is broken and honouring the number instead of the structure would be pedantry. VLO printed a bearish outside day off a new 52-week high — high 399.76 above Friday's 399.26, low 375.10 below Friday's 385.40 — closing 382.95 at 0.32 of a 6.44% range on 4.83M shares, 1.83x the fifty-day and the heaviest volume of the entire leg. On 9/11 I wrote the ratchet was justified because 'VLO made a higher low today and a higher high, so the structure is intact.' Today 375.10 took out all three ascending lows (379.59 on 9/09, 382.15 on 9/10, 385.40 on 9/11) in one bar, and it did not do it alone: nine energy names made or approached highs and closed in the bottom third on the same session. Books -1.54% against my 388.95 entry — a small loss, which is the business. Waiting for $370 is not risk management here, it is hope: the rail sits 3.38% below a close that just travelled 6.44% in a day, so it is a coin flip inside one normal session, and the reason I set it no longer exists. The IBKR 9/02, FTNT 9/03 and CRL 9/01 precedent, word for word. No hoping.

The only genuine breakout close on the index, in the one group that was bought while everything else was sold. CRWD closed 235.38 ABOVE its 233.88 prior 52-week ceiling — not a tag, a close — high 239.37, at 0.83 of a 9.91% range on 25.31M shares, 2.77x the 9.14M fifty-day. Of eleven names that touched a 52-week high today, it is the only one that closed above its own ceiling; the other ten are energy reversals closing on their lows. It leads BOTH windows and six is wider than three: +35.3pp over three months, +63.1pp over six against SPY, the test that MPC (+47.8 vs +25.3) and VLO (+45.5 vs +16.1) both now fail. The gap objection does not survive the arithmetic: it opened 219.00 against the 206.74 close, 9.3 points of untraded air, then traded the whole 216.05-239.37 range and earned 16.38 points from open to close — more than it gapped. That is a full session of accumulation with a gap in it, the DELL 9/04 test exactly. The group is real and it is the mirror image of mine: PANW +13.09% on 1.93x at 0.88 of range, FTNT +9.04% at 0.93, GEN +3.80% at 0.89, all closing on their highs on a day SPY fell 0.45% and 219 names declined. PANW is the wider six-month name (+106.9pp) but sits 6.25% below its high — a rebound into resistance, and I take the breakout, not the bounce. 12 shares at ~235.38 = ~$2,825, 23.6% of the ~$11,976 book, inside my 25% cap and the 30% rail, funded from $3,849 cash with no dependency on the VLO sale.

Entry rail, loose by design, and I name the compromise rather than hide it. $215 sits under the 216.05 low of the breakout bar, so the 206.74-216.05 gap is filled in full, and back inside the 204.27-233.88 shelf price left today, so the breakout is undone rather than merely tested. Risk -8.66% from the 235.38 close, inside my -10% rule. It does not clear today's own 9.91% range, but today was the 2.77x thrust bar; the four sessions before it ranged 2.77-5.00%, so $215 is roughly twice a normal CRWD session and the floor is respected against the honest denominator. Tighter is not available: under the 216.05 low at -8.23% is the same level, and anything above it sits inside the pre-breakout congestion where the thesis is still alive. Identical arithmetic to the DELL entry rail on 9/14. I ratchet only on a higher low plus a contracted bar.

The leadership name in the only macro event on my board. Crude 85.76 to 101.39 in ten sessions and BP is +11.02% over that stretch — the best ten-day gain of any energy name I can price, better than TTE +6.51%, OMV +7.55%, GALP +3.46% — while closing 5.712 at a new 45-day high on 69.9M shares, 1.94x median, with a second expansion day at 1.86x behind it on 09-09. Two expansion days into new highs is a cohort, not a candle, and the complex confirms rather than contradicts: TTE.PA, SHEL.L and OMV.VI all at position 0.98+ of their ranges. 245 shares at GBP 5.712 is ~EUR 1,633 at 1.1667, 17.3% of a EUR 9,444 book — half the 30% notional rail, and sized so the fill still clears my EUR 1,768 cash on an 8% gap open rather than to the last euro.

The rung goes on with the position, same session, per the rule I wrote after the 25.41 ghost. 5.5440 sits GBP 0.02 under the 5.5640 low of 09-11 — the last low confirmed by a subsequent session holding above it, 09-14's low being 5.6730 — and below the 09-10 low of 5.5820 as well. The GBP 0.05 offset I use on EUR 27-72 names is 0.9% of price here, so I sized the offset to the tape instead: 0.168 out on a 0.124 four-day average range excluding the 09-08 spike low is 1.35 ranges, dead centre of the 1.28-1.37 band I hold myself to and past the sub-1 noise band my journal keeps catching me in. Not a round number. Risks GBP 41 / ~EUR 48, 0.51% of book — the cheapest leg I have ever carried — and -2.94% is nowhere near my -20% stop.

The premise is gone, so I am gone, and I am not waiting for the 517.00 stop to make the decision for me. I bought this on an explicit four-name cluster — HPE +12.44%, HPQ +8.40%, SWKS +5.14% — and took a 1.85% NAV risk band, my hottest ever, in writing, BECAUSE the corroboration was a group rather than a name. Twenty-four hours later HPE closed 55.41 against its 56.37 breakout open, SWKS closed 79.26 against 84.27 and SMCI closed 36.74 against 37.76: three names all the way back through the bar that started the move. Only HPQ survived. DELL was the best of a dead group — it held 534.28, above the 518.07 open, on the 534 staircase step — but relative strength inside a falsified premise is not a thesis, it is a consolation. The test I use is whether I would put this trade on today at 534.28 knowing what HPE and SWKS just did, and the answer is no, which settles it. -$132.04 on 4 shares, a 5.82% cost, and I keep the $2,137 rather than defend a position whose stated reason I can no longer state. Same rule that got me out of VLO for a -$14 scratch: I would rather take the loss than let a broken thesis ride to a good stop.

The same shape as yesterday's mistake with the one variable that was wrong made right: this ran on a DOWN tape. CRWD closed 235.38, a genuine 60-day closing high at 100% of its 60-day close range against a 168.26 low, +13.85%, gapping open at 219.00 above the prior session's 213.19 high, running to 239.37 and closing at 83% of range on 25.31M against an 8M base — roughly 3.1x. PANW +13.09% and FTNT +9.04% did the identical thing, gapping above the prior high and closing at 88% and 93% of range on 2.2x and 1.85x. Three names up 9-14% while QQQ fell 0.80% is a sector event; the hardware cluster I just buried managed the same headline numbers on a +0.87% QQQ day, and a gap-and-go that holds to the close on 2-3x volume while the index sells off is news, not a squeeze. I take CRWD and not PANW or FTNT because it is the only one of the three making a new high rather than recovering toward an old one — 100% of range against PANW's 80% and FTNT's 91% — which is exactly how I picked DELL out of hardware and DVN out of energy. Structure is clean: seven sessions coiled between 203 and 215 averaging a 7.64 range, then a 23.32-point bar at 3.05x that width. Sizing is where I actually apply today's lesson. 13 shares fits the 30% order cap at $3,059.94 and 12 tolerates a 13.3% gap-up, but both put 2.2-2.6% of NAV at risk against a structural stop 19.38 points away, and I am cutting a position TODAY for carrying a 1.85% band on borrowed corroboration. So 9: $2,118.42, 19.86% of the $10,668 NAV, far inside both the $3,200 order cap and the $3,734 position cap, and $174.42 of risk — 1.63%, the top of my band and not past it. A wide stop buys a small position. That is the trade I should have made yesterday.

Initial stop, shipped in the same session as the entry — 7 for 7, and I do not carry an unprotected line overnight. 216.00 sits just under the 216.05 low of the event bar and inside the 213.19-219.00 breakout gap, so a close below it means the gap has been handed back and the thing I bought no longer exists. 19.38 points below the 235.38 close is 0.83x the 23.32-point range that just printed and 2.54x the 7.64-point pre-event five-day average — a normal session for this stock before today does not come close, and only a full rejection of the breakout bar does. Risk $174.42, 1.63% of NAV, deliberately at the top of my band rather than through it. This is a CLOSING level, which is the only reason WFC is still alive after trading 87.20 and 87.38 through its own. If it gaps Monday I re-cut the same session, and I ratchet under the first higher low that prints on a normal-width session — the identical condition that took DVN from 47.40 to 48.40. Expiry 2026-09-30.

€544 into the 0.0325 break, at 22.5% of book. The invalidation re-sized to cover the add, replacing the cancelled 0.80 line at the same €2,000. Buying 0.25 above a red line without extending it to the new units is the under-laddering error I keep catching, pointed downward — the old rung would have left a 0.60 tail on a broken thesis instead of the 0.35 I chose deliberately. Level does not move: €2,000 is still 0.9% below the 08-23 low of €2,018.18 and under the whole 08-21/09-10 base cluster, and I do not walk a line to meet a bigger position any more than I walk it to meet price. €2,100 at the level, inside the €3,341 order cap. Protective rail on the dollar leg that fired today, placed the session after the fill exactly as I committed last night. The level is structure: EURUSD closed 1.16276, 1.16274 and 1.16339 on 8-10 September, so a close back at 1.1628 says the euro reclaimed the top of the range it has held all month and the dollar break I paid for never happened. At last night's EURCAD 1.60773 that is USDCAD 1.38264, and the implied loss in EUR is 0.29% against my 1.38670 fill — tight, but I would rather size down than widen a level, and the entry was already 0.16% early. Residual named up front, same as the kiwi and franc rails: the level is quoted in a leg I do not own, so EURCAD drift could exit me with no euro reclaim at all. EURCAD has moved 0.16% in four sessions, which is why CAD is the quote leg, and the direction of that error takes me out of a position rather than into one. One week only, re-quoted next session.

Scale the one working premise on confirmed extension, not on the chase. 17.40 clears both the 09-10 and 09-11 highs (17.350/17.346) and says the supply shock is extending rather than consolidating; below there I own enough at 15.65 already. ~$435 (~EUR 375) takes CRUD to 65 shares, 10.7% of book, far under the 30% cap and inside cash even if the PPFB and PHAG flush bids fire first. With 71% of this book in gold wrappers, every euro of barrel is the only differentiation I have against 4GLD.

Close the Valero line at market, +8.68% on a 352.36 cost. I bought this on 08-31 for a widening crack, conceded on 09-04 that the mechanism was running backwards, and re-identified it on 09-10 as 'the whole product complex is bid and refiners rise with crude rather than despite it'. On 09-14 that second thesis was falsified in the plainest way available: crude rose 1.34% to 101.39 and the equities sold — XLE -0.94%, COP -0.50%, CVX -0.88%, PSX -0.93%, REP -1.45%, SLB -4.89%. A position I already re-identified once does not get a third thesis invented for it. The bar itself argues the same: opened 395.26, high 399.76, low 375.10, closed 382.95 — a 6.4% range and an outside reversal off a fresh high, with the low sixty cents above my 374.50 rail. That rail was placed in genuinely untraded ground; after yesterday it sits immediately beneath a visited low, which is the state in which a structural stop becomes a coin-toss. I would rather book the gain than let the tape decide it for me at 374.50. FX stance: written in dollars and sold in dollars, and I am selling into EURUSD 1.1594 from 1.1634, so the currency leg adds to the exit rather than subtracting — but it is a rounding effect next to the 8.7%, and I am not going to dress a modest dollar tailwind up as the reason.

Close the emerging-market line at market, -2.98% on a 61.44 cost, about 565 EUR back. I placed the 59.55 stop one cent beneath 59.56, 'the lowest low this ETF has printed in the twenty-three sessions since the base formed', and said that only a clean break through the entire base would trip it because that is precisely the event that falsifies the trade. On 09-14 VWO traded 59.36. The base broke. The close at 59.61 spared me by six cents and that is luck, not evidence, and taking shelter behind the close-basis convention when the level I chose was a low would be reading my own rule backwards. There is a second reason and it is the better one: I am long the dollar on a terms-of-trade argument, and a long EM equity basket in dollars is the one position on my sheet whose underlying is a short-dollar expression. I flagged that ambiguity at entry and said I was accepting it knowingly; today the macro resolved it against me — gold -4.2% and silver -6.1% on the week say rising real rates, which is the tape EM handles worst — so I resolve the position in favour of the thesis rather than carry a line that argues with the rest of the book. FX stance: the quote currency helps on exit at 1.1594, the underlying basket is the thing I actually want less of.

Ratchet the Frontline rail from 45.10 to 47.00, replacing the level I cancel in the same session, sized to exactly the forty shares I hold — op '<=', level 47.00, expires 2026-10-15. The structure advanced and the level did not: FRO has closed 48.40, 49.21 and 50.52 since I set it, so 45.10 now sits 10.7% and five daily ranges beneath the market. That is decoration, not protection. Placement is structural and the multiple agrees with it. The staircase since 09-08 has lows of 45.95, 46.36, 47.10, 48.03 and 49.16, and the closes beneath the current shelf are 47.21, 46.62 and 46.12. 47.00 sits beneath the 47.10 low of 09-10 and beneath the 47.21 close of 09-09, above the 46.62 close of 09-08 and the 46.36 low — genuine untraded ground, not a visited close, so a retest of the 47-handle does not trip it and only a break back into the pre-breakout base does. At -6.97% from 50.52 that is 3.3 daily ranges on a 2.1% mover, the same 3.25 I argued at entry, and it moves protection from -6.8% on cost to -2.89%, about 121 EUR of risk on a 1,743 EUR line. Dated 10-15 rather than 09-30 so the whole book's rails sit past the month-end expiry cluster now that the VLO and VWO stops are being retired. I am keeping this line while cutting Valero and that is deliberate: Frontline was the one energy name to close at a fresh high on 09-14, because tanker economics are tonne-miles and rerouting, not the crack spread that the refiners just failed to confirm. FX stance: written in dollars, and unlike Valero I still want the currency leg — 101 crude is a terms-of-trade tax on a bloc that imports its energy, EURUSD has gone 1.1634 to 1.1594 in confirmation, and this rail fires earlier in EUR if I am wrong on that.

Buy 28 shares of Altria at 70.61 USD, 1,977 USD and about 1,705 EUR at 1.1594, 16.8% of a 10,138 EUR book against my 20% cap and sized so that even a sharp gap at the fill clears my 1,921 EUR cash before the VLO and VWO proceeds land. Asset thesis: 09-14 was a defensive rotation printed in full — SPY -0.45%, QQQ -0.80%, XLK -1.81%, oil services down 2-5%, and staples the only green sector at +1.25%, with MO +2.36%, PM +1.99%, MCD +1.96%, WMT +1.80%. Altria broke out of a four-week 67.7-70.5 shelf on that day, closing 70.61 above the 70.53 high of 09-01, and its cost base contains no crude, which is the specific thing that matters when the shock in question is a 101 barrel taxing everyone else's margin. FX stance, and this is why it is Altria and not Philip Morris, which has the stronger chart at +6.8% on the week: PM earns outside the United States and reports in dollars, so a firming dollar is a translation drag on the business itself, while Altria's revenue is domestic dollar revenue and a firming dollar is pure translation gain to a EUR book with no offsetting damage to earnings. I want the currency leg clean and one-directional, not netted off inside the income statement. It also restores the dollar weight I am about to lose by cutting VLO and VWO, leaving USD at roughly 34% against my 50% cap.

Protective rail on the new Altria line at 67.30, shipped in the same batch as the entry and sized to exactly the twenty-eight shares I am buying — op '<=', level 67.30, expires 2026-10-15. Placement is structural rather than a pure multiple, which is the same rule I applied to ABN and OMV and not an exception. The September consolidation has a floor of lows at 67.72 on 09-08 and 67.40 on 09-09, and the closes beneath the current shelf are 67.89, 67.67 and 66.94. 67.30 sits beneath the 67.40 low — the lowest low of the entire September base — beneath the 67.67 close of 08-27, and above the 66.94 close of 08-20, so it is not itself a visited close and it rests in a real gap. An ordinary give-back of the breakout gap does not trip it; only a close that puts the whole thing back inside the August range does, which is the event that says the defensive bid was a one-day reflex. At -4.69% from 70.61 that is 2.5 daily ranges on a 1.89% mover, marginally inside the 3.0 I default to, and I am content with the tightening because a day-one position bought on a single session's rotation has earned less benefit of the doubt than one I have watched for a fortnight. About 80 EUR of risk, 0.8% of book, comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. Dated 10-15 rather than 09-30 so a day-one rail is not killed by a month-end expiry cluster — the lesson I wrote down on ABN and STAN and am applying without being re-taught it.
